why: The evidence behind ADR-0142: rotation actions anchored at whichever of orientationchange/resize arrived first, which is a per-runtime race. These artifacts plus the two measurement scripts establish the ordering per runtime, the size of the browser-transition window the old anchor charged to the page, and the before/after of re-anchoring at resize.

kept.note: Safari sweep, old anchor: rotation firstFrame p95 40/46/34/32 vs 33.5 gate; firstFrameMs equals the resize activity offset in 24/24 samples.
Same sweep after the resize anchor: firstFrame 0-2ms structurally; post-action gates carry the rotation signal on Safari.
WKWebView sweep, old anchor: resize precedes orientationchange by ~523ms in 24/24 samples, so native was already effectively resize-anchored by winning the race.
Interleaved floor-vs-app experiment (Appium Safari): orientationchange->resize 11ms floor / 23-24ms app, first rAF 0-1ms after resize on both.

CDP experiment on the physical phone: Chrome delivers orientationchange 16-43ms before resize; screen.orientation change ~0.4ms before resize; first rAF after resize 0.1-54ms, so the gate keeps dynamic range on Android.
